tos-1x09: Nurse Chapel finds her lost fiancé Roger Korby on Exo III, but he plans to seed the galaxy with android duplicates, starting with Kirk, and is one himself.
tos-1x10: At the Tantalus V penal colony, Kirk and Dr. Helen Noel find Dr. Tristan Adams's celebrated neural neutralizer empties and reshapes minds, as Spock mind-melds with a victim.
tos-1x11: A longevity experiment has killed every adult on an Earth-duplicate planet, and when the landing party catches the disease, McCoy races for a cure among centuries-old children.
tos-1x12: Kirk suspects touring actor Anton Karidian is Kodos the Executioner, who slaughtered thousands on Tarsus IV, as the surviving witnesses, Kirk among them, are targeted one by one.
tos-1x13: When the shuttle Galileo crashes on Taurus II, Spock's first command falters as giant creatures pick off his crew, until a desperate fuel flare catches the Enterprise's eye.
tos-1x14: Kirk stands trial for the death of officer Ben Finney, damned by computer records, until Spock proves they were doctored by Finney himself, alive and hiding aboard.
tos-1x15: Spock hijacks the Enterprise with the crippled Christopher Pike aboard, locking its heading for forbidden Talos IV, and faces a court-martial that replays Pike's first visit there.
tos-1x16: Spock's court-martial plays out through Talosian images of Pike's captivity, and the true purpose emerges: to give the crippled Pike an illusory life on Talos IV with Vina.
tos-1x17: On an idyllic shore-leave planet, the crew's passing thoughts take solid form, from a white rabbit to Kirk's old Academy tormentor, in an amusement park built by aliens.
tos-1x18: The Enterprise is held captive by Trelane, a playful, all-powerful being with a taste for Earth's past glories, until his unseen parents call him away.
tos-1x19: After the Gorn destroy the Cestus III outpost, the Metrons pit Kirk against the Gorn captain in single combat, and Kirk builds a crude cannon but chooses mercy.
tos-1x20: A rift between universes brings Lazarus, a man locked in endless war with his antimatter double, and Kirk must trap them both between realities to avert total annihilation.
tos-1x21: Flung back to 1969 by a black star, the Enterprise beams aboard Air Force pilot John Christopher, then must return him and erase every trace of its visit.
tos-1x22: On Beta III, a docile population broken only by the violent Red Hour obeys the unseen Landru, a centuries-old computer that Kirk talks into destroying itself.
tos-1x23: Eminiar VII fights Vendikar by computer simulation, with the listed dead reporting to disintegration chambers, and when the Enterprise is counted among them, Kirk smashes the war computers.
tos-1x24: Revived from the sleeper ship Botany Bay, Khan Noonien Singh and his engineered supermen seize the Enterprise, and Kirk, after retaking it, exiles them to Ceti Alpha V.
tos-1x25: On Omicron Ceti III, spores that bring perfect contentment seduce the crew and even Spock, who finds love with Leila Kalomi, until Kirk discovers anger breaks their hold.
tos-1x26: A creature killing miners on Janus VI turns out, through Spock's mind-meld, to be the Horta, a mother defending the eggs the miners have been unknowingly destroying.
tos-1x27: On Organia, Kirk and Spock urge its placid people to resist Kor's Klingon occupiers, then learn the Organians are energy beings who end the war themselves.
tos-1x28: An overdosed McCoy alters history through the Guardian of Forever, and Kirk, pursuing him into 1930 New York, falls for Edith Keeler, whose death he must allow.
tos-1x29: Flying parasites drive the colonists of Deneva mad, killing Kirk's brother Sam, and after Spock is infected, the crew learns intense light can destroy the creatures.
tos-2x01: On Pyris VII, the alien explorers Korob and Sylvia greet the landing party with witches, a haunted castle, and a black cat, illusions drawn from humanity's darkest fears.
tos-2x02: Kirk's shuttle is drawn to an asteroid where Zefram Cochrane, the long-vanished inventor of warp drive, lives kept young by the Companion, an energy being who loves him.
tos-2x03: Negotiating for mining rights on Capella IV against a Klingon rival, Kirk, Spock, and McCoy end up protecting Eleen, the pregnant widow of the planet's murdered ruler.
tos-2x04: The being once worshipped on Earth as Apollo grips the Enterprise with a giant energy hand, demands the crew's devotion, and courts Lieutenant Carolyn Palamas as his queen.
tos-2x05: Gripped by pon farr, Spock must return to Vulcan to marry T'Pring, who invokes a ritual challenge that forces Kirk to fight his friend to the death.
tos-2x06: Commodore Matt Decker, sole survivor of the Constellation, commandeers the Enterprise to avenge his crew on a planet-killing machine, and Kirk destroys it with Decker's wrecked ship.
tos-2x07: Accused of murdering women on Argelius II, Scotty is cleared when the killer proves to be Redjac, a fear-feeding entity that once stalked London as Jack the Ripper.
tos-2x08: The ancient Earth probe Nomad, merged with an alien sterilizer, mistakes Kirk for its creator and purges imperfection, until Kirk talks it into destroying itself for its errors.
tos-2x09: The ageless natives of lush Gamma Trianguli VI serve the machine god Vaal, which attacks the landing party, and Kirk frees the people by destroying it.
tos-2x10: Swept into a mirror universe by a transporter accident, Kirk, Uhura, McCoy, and Scott must pass as officers of a ruthless empire, aided by a bearded, calculating Spock.
tos-2x11: Radiation on Gamma Hydra IV ages Kirk, Scott, McCoy, and Spock decades in days, and the key to a cure lies with Chekov, the one officer spared.
tos-2x12: An android named Norman hijacks the Enterprise to a planet of androids ruled in name by Harry Mudd, and the crew escapes by overloading the machines with illogic.
tos-2x13: Guarding grain at Space Station K-7, Kirk contends with a pompous official, brawling Klingons, and fast-breeding tribbles, which end up exposing poisoned grain and a Klingon spy.
tos-2x14: On a planet where Rome never fell, Captain Merik of the lost Beagle, now an imperial officer, sends Kirk, Spock, and McCoy toward death in televised gladiator games.
tos-2x15: Ferrying delegates to Babel, the Enterprise carries Spock's estranged father Sarek, suspected of murder and dying, and Spock must choose between command and giving blood to save him.
tos-2x16: Finding Klingons arming one faction of a peaceful people on Neural, Kirk grimly decides to supply matching weapons to protect his friend Tyree's tribe.
tos-2x17: Snatched away to Triskelion, Kirk, Uhura, and Chekov become trained gladiators for the Providers, disembodied brains who bet on them, until Kirk wagers everyone's freedom.
tos-2x18: Kirk becomes fixated on killing a vampiric cloud creature that ravaged the Farragut's crew years ago, and hunts it with Ensign Garrovick, son of the captain it killed.
tos-2x19: Once Spock senses the death of the Vulcan-crewed Intrepid, the Enterprise finds a giant energy-eating amoeba about to reproduce, and Spock pilots a shuttle into it.
tos-2x20: The Iotians have modeled their entire society on a book about 1920s Chicago mobs left by an earlier ship, so Kirk plays gangster to unite the rival bosses.
tos-2x21: Kelvans from Andromeda seize the Enterprise and shrink most of the crew into blocks, leaving Kirk and three officers to turn the invaders' borrowed human senses against them.
tos-2x22: Sargon and two fellow survivors of an ancient race borrow Kirk, Spock, and Dr. Ann Mulhall's bodies to build android forms, until Henoch refuses to give Spock's back.
tos-2x23: Searching for historian John Gill on Ekos, Kirk and Spock find he has modeled the planet on Nazi Germany, and his regime is now persecuting the neighboring Zeons.
tos-2x24: Richard Daystrom's M-5 computer is installed to run the Enterprise, then turns war games into real attacks on Starfleet ships until Kirk convinces it it has committed murder.
tos-2x25: The Exeter's crew lies dead of a plague, and on Omega IV Kirk finds its captain, Ron Tracey, arming the Kohms against the Yangs in search of immortality.
tos-2x26: Researching history in 1968, the Enterprise crew runs into Gary Seven, an agent of unseen aliens, as he and his cat Isis sabotage an orbital nuclear warhead launch.
tos-3x01: Cast by the Melkotians as the doomed Clanton gang, Kirk and four officers must relive the O.K. Corral shootout until a mind-meld convinces them the bullets are unreal.
tos-3x02: Escorting the imperious Elaan of Elas to wed the ruler of rival Troyius, Kirk falls under the spell of her tears as a Klingon ship stalks them.
tos-3x03: Stripped of his memory, Kirk lives as Kirok among transplanted Native Americans and marries Miramanee, while Spock races to stop an asteroid from striking their planet.
tos-3x04: Feigning instability, Kirk crosses into Romulan territory as cover for a secret mission: while Spock distracts the Romulan commander, a disguised Kirk steals her cloaking device.
tos-3x05: Orphaned children from the Triacus colony, under the sway of the malevolent Gorgan, take over the Enterprise, until Kirk breaks the spell by making them face their grief.
tos-3x06: Kara, leader of a planet's cave-dwelling women, steals Spock's brain to run their underground machinery, and McCoy, boosted by an alien teaching device, must put it back.
tos-3x07: Blind telepath Dr. Miranda Jones escorts Kollos, a Medusan ambassador whose appearance drives humans mad, and her jealousy of Spock nearly costs him his mind.
tos-3x08: The Vians torture Kirk, Spock, and McCoy as the Minara sun nears nova, testing whether Gem, a mute empath, will risk her life to heal them.
tos-3x09: Kirk vanishes into interspace with the derelict Defiant, and as the Tholians spin an energy web around the Enterprise, Spock and McCoy clash while trying to retrieve him.
tos-3x10: Dying of an incurable illness, McCoy falls for Natira, priestess of Yonada, an asteroid ship whose unwitting people are headed for impact with a populated planet.
tos-3x11: An energy being that feeds on hatred traps the crew and Kang's Klingons in endless sword-fighting, until both sides refuse to fight and laugh it off the ship.
tos-3x12: Psychokinetic followers of Plato force Kirk, Spock, Uhura, and Chapel to perform humiliating spectacles, until McCoy traces their powers to kironide and the crew gains them too.
tos-3x13: Hyperaccelerated Scalosians, moving too fast to be seen, seize the Enterprise to breed with its crew, and their queen Deela speeds Kirk up to be her mate.
tos-3x14: Stranded on a planet built by the vanished Kalandans, Kirk's landing party is hunted by a lethal computer projection of Losira, the outpost's long-dead commander.
tos-3x15: Two Cherons, Lokai and his pursuer Bele, drag the Enterprise into their feud over which side of their faces is black, even after learning their world is dead.
tos-3x16: At the Elba II asylum, shape-shifting former hero Garth of Izar takes over and holds Kirk and Spock captive, scheming to seize the Enterprise and conquer the galaxy.
tos-3x17: Beamed onto an empty replica of the Enterprise, Kirk meets Odona, whose overcrowded world Gideon wants the disease in his blood to thin its population.
tos-3x18: Energy beings from Zetar, last remnants of a dead people, ravage the Memory Alpha library planetoid and try to possess Lieutenant Mira Romaine, the woman Scotty loves.
tos-3x19: Needing zenite to stop a plague, Kirk finds the cloud city Stratos oppressing the Troglyte miners below, whose supposed inferiority comes from the mineral's toxic gas.
tos-3x20: Dropouts who reject technology, led by the fanatical Dr. Sevrin, hijack the Enterprise to reach the legendary planet Eden, which proves beautiful but lethally poisonous.
tos-3x21: Seeking a plague cure, Kirk meets Flint, an immortal who once lived as da Vinci and Brahms, and falls for Rayna, the android Flint built as his companion.
tos-3x22: Rock-like Excalbians stage a battle of good against evil, pitting Kirk, Spock, Abraham Lincoln, and Surak against re-creations of Kahless, Genghis Khan, and other infamous villains.
tos-3x23: Through a time portal on doomed Sarpeidon, Kirk lands in a witch-hunting past while Spock and McCoy reach an ice age, where Spock falls for the exile Zarabeth.
tos-3x24: Kirk's former lover Janice Lester swaps bodies with him to take the Enterprise, and only Spock, after a mind-meld, believes the real captain is trapped in her body.
voy-1x01-02: Hauled into the Delta Quadrant with the Maquis ship it was chasing, Voyager forfeits a quick trip home when Janeway destroys the Caretaker's array to protect the Ocampa.
voy-1x03: Voyager's own reflected distress call lures it into a quantum singularity's event horizon, and B'Elanna Torres wins the chief engineer's post by helping get the ship out.
voy-1x04: Surveying a world wiped out by a polaric explosion, Janeway and Paris slip back a day and find their own rescue attempt may cause the disaster.
voy-1x05: Vidiian organ harvesters, ravaged by a disease called the phage, steal Neelix's lungs, and the Doctor keeps him alive with holographic ones until Kes donates a lung.
voy-1x06: Voyager's search for energy inside a nebula wounds what turns out to be a living organism, and Janeway takes the ship back in to heal it.
voy-1x07: A tiny wormhole connects Voyager to a Romulan ship in the Alpha Quadrant, but the scientist aboard, Telek R'Mor, is living twenty years in the past.
voy-1x08: Convicted on Banea of murdering a scientist, Tom Paris is sentenced to relive the killing through the victim's eyes, until Tuvok proves the memories were planted for espionage.
voy-1x09: Pulled through a subspace rift to the Vhnori homeworld, Harry Kim challenges their belief in an afterlife by describing the asteroid where their dead end up.
voy-1x10: The pleasure-loving Sikarians own a spatial trajector that could fling Voyager 40,000 light-years toward home, but refuse to share it, tempting Tuvok and Torres into a secret trade.
voy-1x11: When Voyager technology turns up aboard a Kazon ship, the hunt for a traitor exposes Seska, a Cardassian agent posing as a Bajoran, who defects to the Kazon.
voy-1x12: When crew members vanish within Harry Kim's Beowulf holonovel, the Doctor makes his first away mission and discovers photonic aliens are taking them.
voy-1x13: With Chakotay left brain-dead, his consciousness leaps between crewmates to steer Voyager away from a nebula where aliens feed on neural energy.
voy-1x14: A Vidiian scientist hunting a phage cure splits B'Elanna Torres into a human woman and a Klingon one, who must rely on each other to escape.
voy-1x15: Jetrel, whose weapon killed hundreds of thousands of Talaxians on Rinax, claims Neelix may be ill as cover for an attempt to restore the dead.
voy-1x16: Tuvok puts four undisciplined Maquis crewmen through Starfleet training, while the ship's bio-neural circuitry falls sick with an infection traced to Neelix's cheese.
voy-2x01: A Ford pickup from 1936, adrift in space, leads Voyager to Amelia Earhart and other humans abducted in 1937, whose descendants now thrive on a distant planet.
voy-2x02: Chakotay is attacked during a solo ritual by Kar, a Kazon youth who must kill an enemy to earn his name, and tries to show him another way.
voy-2x03: Damaged by a radiation surge, the Doctor is told by a holographic Reginald Barclay that he is really his own creator, Lewis Zimmerman, trapped in a Voyager simulation.
voy-2x04: Space-dwelling creatures draw Voyager into their mating rituals, while their energy triggers Kes's elogium, the Ocampa's one chance to conceive, forcing her and Neelix to decide on parenthood.
voy-2x05: Harry Kim wakes in San Francisco beside his fiancée Libby, in a timeline where he never joined Voyager, and must re-create the shuttle accident that put him there.
voy-2x06: A distortion ring engulfs Voyager and rearranges its corridors into a shrinking maze, and the crew's only way out is to stop fighting it and wait.
voy-2x07: Feuding over Kes, Paris and Neelix are stranded together on a hostile planet, where caring for a newly hatched reptilian creature forces them to work out their differences.
voy-2x08: An exhausted Janeway and her crew are overwhelmed by hallucinations drawn from their memories and fantasies, and only Kes can resist the telepathic alien behind them.
voy-2x09: A symbol matching Chakotay's tribal markings leads him to the Sky Spirits, aliens who shaped his ancestors, stirring memories of a youthful jungle trek with his father.
voy-2x10: Searching for the Caretaker's mate, Suspiria, Voyager finds an Ocampa colony whose leader, Tanis, trains Kes to amplify her mental powers toward sinister ends.
voy-2x11: After Seska helps the Kazon steal a transporter module, Chakotay pursues them alone and is captured and tortured, and Seska secretly takes his DNA to conceive a child.
voy-2x12: To free Tuvok and Torres from the Mokra, Janeway accepts help from Caylem, a delusional old rebel who believes she is his long-lost daughter.
voy-2x13: A robot Torres revives, Automated Unit 3947, abducts her to build more of its kind, and she learns its race killed its makers and wages endless war.
voy-2x14: Battered by Kazon attacks, Janeway seeks allies, first among the Kazon and then with their former masters, the Trabe, whose leader turns peace talks into an ambush.
voy-2x15: In a modified shuttle, Tom Paris breaks the warp 10 barrier, but the feat starts mutating him into a new species, and he abducts Janeway, who changes too.
voy-2x16: To understand why crewman Lon Suder killed a shipmate for no reason, Tuvok mind-melds with him and absorbs his violent impulses, losing his own emotional control.
voy-2x17: Torres's old Maquis project, a reprogrammed Cardassian missile called Dreadnought, turns up in the Delta Quadrant targeting a populated world, and she must outthink her own programming.
voy-2x18: Freed from a comet prison, a Q called Quinn requests asylum in order to die, and Janeway must rule on his plea as Q argues against it.
voy-2x19: The Doctor falls for Danara Pel, a Vidiian physician whose mind he places in a healthy holographic body while treating her, as Tom Paris grows openly insubordinate.
voy-2x20: Using his new shipboard news program, Neelix investigates Tom Paris's sudden departure and uncovers both Paris's undercover mission and the real traitor, Michael Jonas.
voy-2x21: A spatial rift duplicates Voyager, and when Vidiians overrun one copy, its Janeway destroys it to save the other, which takes in its Harry Kim and a newborn.
voy-2x22: Stranded on a moon, Tuvok protects frightened children who keep disappearing, then learns they are Drayan elders nearing death in a species that ages backward.
voy-2x23: Trying to wake survivors from stasis pods, Harry Kim and Torres are trapped in a virtual world ruled by a sadistic clown, the embodiment of the sleepers' fear.
voy-2x24: A transporter accident merges Tuvok and Neelix into Tuvix, and when a way to separate them is found, Janeway must end a life that begs to continue.
voy-2x25: Infected with a virus only their new planet holds at bay, Janeway and Chakotay settle into a life together, until Tuvok defies orders to get a Vidiian cure.
voy-2x26: Seska's claim that she has borne Chakotay's son draws Voyager into a Kazon-Nistrim ambush, and Culluh seizes the ship and maroons its crew on a primitive world.
voy-3x01: Marooned on Hanon IV, the crew fights natives and predators to survive, while Lon Suder and the Doctor sabotage the Kazon aboard Voyager and Paris brings help.
voy-3x02: A mind-meld meant to cure Tuvok's hallucinations takes Janeway into his years on Captain Sulu's Excelsior, where a memory virus has lurked for decades.
voy-3x03: Wrongly jailed for an Akritirian bombing, Tom Paris and Harry Kim land in a brutal prison where a neural clamp slowly drives inmates mad, testing their friendship.
voy-3x04: Voyager cuts through territory guarded by an alien swarm while the Doctor's program begins to degrade, forcing Kes and a holographic copy of his creator to save him.
voy-3x05: Arridor and Kol, Ferengi stranded by the Barzan wormhole, rule a primitive world as revered sages, and Voyager must unseat them beside an unstable wormhole leading home.
voy-3x06: While Voyager ferries Enaran passengers, Torres dreams through the eyes of a young Enaran who saw her people wipe out a dissident group, a genocide they have erased.
voy-3x07: When Kes collapses after trespassing in a Nechani shrine, Janeway undergoes the monks' baffling spiritual trials to save her, setting aside her trust in science.
voy-3x08: Attacked by a 29th-century timeship, Voyager is thrown back to 1996 Los Angeles, where tech mogul Henry Starling has built his fortune on salvaged future technology.
voy-3x09: Before Henry Starling can fly his stolen timeship into the future and devastate it, Janeway must stop him, aided by astronomer Rain Robinson and a newly mobile Doctor.
voy-3x10: The dying Ilari warlord Tieran transfers his mind into Kes, using her body to seize power on his homeworld, while Kes fights to reclaim herself.
voy-3x11: Hoping a child will end the Continuum's civil war, Q proposes having one with Janeway, who is drawn into the conflict and steers him toward a female Q.
voy-3x12: Returning from a trade mission, Janeway finds Voyager overrun by giant airborne viruses, and she and the Doctor must fight through the crippled ship to spread an antigen.
voy-3x13: Afraid of becoming useless as Voyager enters space he doesn't know, Neelix joins an old friend's shady deal, which turns deadly and buries him in lies.
voy-3x14: Harry Kim falls for holodeck character Marayna, who prefers Tuvok and proves to be the avatar of a lonely alien seizing control of Voyager from a nearby nebula.
voy-3x15: Caught in repeated deaths after a shuttle crash, Janeway is urged toward the afterlife by her father, until she recognizes him as an alien preying on her mind.
voy-3x16: Vorik's pon farr spreads to B'Elanna Torres, who turns her fevered attentions on Tom Paris during an away mission that ends with the discovery of a dead Borg.
voy-3x17: Nursed by former Borg drones on a war-torn world, Chakotay learns his rescuers want to link minds, his included, into a new collective of their own.
voy-3x18: Adding traits of famous historical figures to his program, the Doctor unleashes a violent alter ego, while Kes considers leaving Voyager for Zahir, a charming Mikhal traveler.
voy-3x19: Helping the Nezu fend off asteroid strikes, Tuvok and Neelix are stranded with survivors who must ride an orbital tether to escape, while a killer hides among them.
voy-3x20: Markings and new abilities convince Harry Kim he is a Taresian, but the planet of welcoming women who claim him turns out to harvest the men it lures.
voy-3x21: An elderly Kes slides backward through her future life, witnessing a war with the Krenim and a family with Tom Paris, toward her own birth.
voy-3x22: When Torres makes the Doctor's idealized holographic family more realistic, he faces a rebellious son and a dying daughter, while Paris gets trapped probing a subspace vortex.
voy-3x23: Voth scientist Forra Gegen finds proof that his saurian people came from Earth, but Voth leaders defending doctrine force him to recant to spare Chakotay.
voy-3x24: One by one, Voyager's crew is swapped for Nyrians, quiet aliens who take over the ship while moving its people into a sprawling habitat of captive environments.
voy-3x25: Crew members get hooked on a holonovel about a Maquis mutiny, written by Tuvok as a training exercise, until a booby trap left by Seska turns it deadly.
voy-3x26: In Borg space, Voyager finds the Collective being overrun by Species 8472, and Janeway strikes a deal with the Borg: a weapon against the invaders for safe passage.
voy-4x01: With Janeway injured, Chakotay must manage the uneasy alliance with the Borg, whose drone liaison, Seven of Nine, is cut off from the Collective and left aboard Voyager.
voy-4x02: As a resentful Seven of Nine is weaned from the Borg, Kes's mental powers surge beyond control, and she leaves, flinging Voyager years closer to home.
voy-4x03: On the Klingon Day of Honor, Torres and Tom Paris end up adrift in space with failing air and confess their feelings, while Borg-ravaged Caatati refugees demand help.
voy-4x04: Stranded amid a war between the Vori and the Kradin, Chakotay fights beside the Vori and learns to hate their enemy, not realizing he is being carefully indoctrinated.
voy-4x05: The Doctor and Torres answer a distress call from Dejaren, a hologram who loathes organic life and has murdered his ship's crew, as Harry Kim falls for Seven.
voy-4x06: Plagued by flashbacks she takes for a Borg summons, Seven steals a shuttle and finds the wrecked Raven, the ship where she was assimilated as a child.
voy-4x07: Invisible Srivani scientists are secretly experimenting on the crew, and once Seven and the Doctor expose them, a stressed-out Janeway steers between two stars to drive them off.
voy-4x08: Krenim scientist Annorax uses a weapon ship that erases species from history to restore his empire, and the changes leave Voyager battered through a grueling year of attacks.
voy-4x09: With Voyager nearly destroyed and Chakotay and Paris held by Annorax, Janeway rams her ship into his timeship, erasing the whole year and returning him to his wife.
voy-4x10: Arrested by the telepathic Mari after her flash of anger fuels a murder, Torres faces a mind purge while Tuvok uncovers a black market in violent thoughts.
voy-4x11: When raiders steal Voyager's main computer and the Doctor's mobile emitter, Janeway tracks them to a planet where her holographic Leonardo da Vinci now serves the thief.
voy-4x12: Brought back by Seven's nanoprobes eighteen hours after dying, Neelix recalls no Great Forest afterlife, and the loss of his faith drives him toward suicide.
voy-4x13: The crew's nightmares share the same menacing alien, and Chakotay must use lucid dreaming to confront a species that lives in dreams and is trapping them asleep.
voy-4x14: Beamed across an alien relay network to the Prometheus, the Doctor must retake the ship from Romulans with its own EMH, then tells Starfleet that Voyager survives.
voy-4x15: Letters from home arrive through the Hirogen relay network, with news that the Maquis are gone and Janeway's fiancé has married, as Hirogen hunters capture Tuvok and Seven.
voy-4x16: Voyager rescues a Hirogen hunter tracking a stranded member of Species 8472, and when Janeway tries to send the creature home, Seven defies her and hands it over.
voy-4x17: Under the Doctor's guidance, Seven recovers memories of being assaulted by the weapons trader Kovin, but the accusation proves mistaken only after it drives him to his death.
voy-4x18: The Hirogen seize Voyager and implant the crew with false identities, hunting them through holodeck battles from Klingon warfare to occupied France in World War II.
voy-4x19: As the World War II simulation spills beyond the holodeck, Janeway and Seven regain their identities and fight to retake Voyager, offering the Hirogen the holographic technology itself.
voy-4x20: Restless Tom Paris befriends Steth, a test pilot flying a coaxial warp drive, who turns out to be a body thief and swaps appearances with him.
voy-4x21: Janeway follows a secret order to destroy subspace-shattering Omega molecules, while Seven, raised by the Borg to revere Omega as perfection, longs to study it first.
voy-4x22: Kellin, a Ramuran whose people leave no trace in others' memories, seeks asylum and rekindles a forgotten romance with Chakotay, until her people erase her memory instead.
voy-4x23: Seven hundred years on, a Kyrian museum portrays Voyager as a murderous warship, and a reactivated backup of the Doctor fights to correct the record amid Kyrian-Vaskan tensions.
voy-4x24: Desperate for deuterium, Voyager lands on a lethal Demon-class planet, where a sentient silver fluid copies Paris and Kim, and Janeway lets it duplicate the whole crew.
voy-4x25: With the crew in stasis to cross a deadly nebula, Seven and the Doctor run Voyager by themselves, and when his program fails, solitude begins to break her.
voy-4x26: The alien linguist Arturis helps decode Starfleet's message and leads Voyager to the Dauntless, a slipstream ship he built as a trap to deliver them to the Borg.
voy-5x01: Crossing a starless expanse, a guilt-stricken Janeway withdraws from her crew, until they discover Malon freighters dumping toxic waste that is killing the region's hidden inhabitants.
voy-5x02: A transporter accident fuses Seven's nanoprobes with the Doctor's 29th-century emitter, creating One, a gentle advanced Borg who ultimately sacrifices himself to keep the Collective from claiming him.
voy-5x03: While the crew builds the Delta Flyer to reach a probe in a gas giant, Torres numbs her grief for the Maquis with deadly holodeck risks.
voy-5x04: Voyager discovers Species 8472 training infiltrators in a replica of Starfleet Academy, and Chakotay goes undercover there before Janeway negotiates a wary peace.
voy-5x05: While her mother is trapped in the crashed Delta Flyer, Neelix keeps young Naomi Wildman distracted with holodeck fairy tales, reliving his own family's loss.
voy-5x06: Fifteen years after a slipstream flight crashed Voyager on an ice planet, Chakotay and Harry Kim defy Starfleet to send a correction back in time and save everyone.
voy-5x07: A salvaged Borg vinculum infected with an alien virus unleashes the minds of people Seven assimilated, from a Klingon to a frightened child, threatening to shatter her own.
voy-5x08: To remove an alien creature clinging to Torres, the Doctor consults a hologram of Crell Moset, a Cardassian exobiologist whose knowledge came from experiments on Bajorans.
voy-5x09: Demoted and jailed for thirty days, Tom Paris writes his father a letter explaining how he defied Janeway to save an ocean world by sabotaging its oxygen refinery.
voy-5x10: Hiding telepathic refugees from Devore inspectors, Janeway grows close to the charming Inspector Kashyk, who claims he wants to defect, in a game of deception she finally wins.
voy-5x11: Finding gaps in his memory, the Doctor uncovers a deleted crisis in which he saved Harry Kim instead of Ensign Jetal, a choice whose guilt broke his program.
voy-5x12: Photonic aliens mistake Tom Paris's Captain Proton serial for reality and declare war on Chaotica, forcing Janeway to play Arachnia, Queen of the Spider People.
voy-5x13: Stranded in a time-distorted sinkhole, Tuvok, Paris, and the Doctor survive with help from Noss, an alien castaway who falls for Tuvok as he suppresses his feelings.
voy-5x14: A wormhole seemingly leading straight to Earth enthralls the crew, but Seven, Naomi, and the Doctor discover it is the lure of a vast creature that devours ships.
voy-5x15-16: Janeway's raid on a Borg sphere for its transwarp coil plays into the Borg Queen's hands, and Seven surrenders to the Collective to spare Voyager, forcing a rescue.
voy-5x17: Harry Kim defies regulations by falling for Tal, a woman from an isolationist Varro generational ship, and their intimacy leaves him with a glowing biological bond.
voy-5x18: As crew members start breaking down, they discover they are the silver-blood duplicates from the Demon-class planet, and their Voyager disintegrates before they can get back.
voy-5x19: Trapped in chaotic space where physics keeps shifting, Chakotay hears voices he fears are his family's hereditary madness, until he realizes aliens are trying to guide Voyager out.
voy-5x20: Hunted by Hazari bounty hunters, Voyager is offered rescue by the Think Tank, a cabal of brilliant aliens whose price is Seven, and Janeway turns the tables.
voy-5x21: With her temper under scrutiny, Torres boards a leaking Malon freighter to stop a blast that would poison the sector, as a mutated crewman stalks its decks.
voy-5x22: Coaching Seven through her first attempts at dating, the Doctor realizes he has fallen for her himself, while Neelix struggles to keep a visiting ambassador out of trouble.
voy-5x23: Researching her ancestor Shannon O'Donnel, whom family legend credits with building the Millennium Gate, Janeway learns the real story involved a stubborn Indiana bookstore owner in 2000.
voy-5x24: Recruited by the 29th-century timeship Relativity, Seven jumps through Voyager's history to find who planted a bomb aboard, and the saboteur proves to be a future Captain Braxton.
voy-5x25: An intelligent weapon of mass destruction seizes the Doctor's program to complete its mission, and Harry Kim must convince it the war it was built for is over.
voy-5x26: Voyager meets the USS Equinox and its captain, Rudy Ransom, whose crew has survived by killing nucleogenic aliens for fuel, and he flees after stealing Voyager's shield technology.
voy-6x01: Hunting Ransom, Janeway grows ruthless, nearly letting an Equinox crewman die and relieving Chakotay when he objects, until Ransom repents and sacrifices himself to save his remaining crew.
voy-6x02: Three ex-drones confront Seven, who kept their minds linked after a crash years ago, and she frees them knowing they will live only a month.
voy-6x03: Near death after a shuttle accident, Torres rides the Klingon Barge of the Dead toward Gre'thor and learns her mother's soul is condemned because of her dishonor.
voy-6x04: Aliens from the Hierarchy spy on Voyager through the Doctor's program and mistake his heroic daydreams for reality, so he must truly play the command hologram he imagines.
voy-6x05: Tom Paris buys an alien shuttle from a junk dealer and falls under its possessive mind, which calls itself Alice and pulls him toward a deadly particle fountain.
voy-6x06: An attack by cloaked Ba'Neth aliens strips Tuvok of his memories and Vulcan discipline, and Neelix helps him rebuild himself as he discovers unexpected joys.
voy-6x07: Sheltering from the Turei on a scorched planet, Voyager revives the Vaadwaur after nine centuries in stasis, only to learn its new allies are would-be conquerors.
voy-6x08: Inside a graviton ellipse, Voyager finds the Ares IV module, lost with astronaut John Kelly on an early Mars mission, and Seven learns the value of exploration.
voy-6x09: After absorbing Voyager's entire database at once, Seven spins a web of conspiracy theories about why the ship was stranded, turning Janeway and Chakotay against each other.
voy-6x10: Barclay confides in Deanna Troi about his obsession with a holodeck Voyager, then risks his career to open the first live communication link with the lost ship.
voy-6x11: Tom Paris's holographic Irish village of the 1800s becomes the crew's escape as a neutronic storm approaches, and Janeway finds herself falling for its barkeep, Michael Sullivan.
voy-6x12: Trapped above a world where time runs fast, Voyager becomes a fixture in the sky of a civilization that grows from primitive villages to spaceflight and frees it.
voy-6x13: The music-less Qomar make the Doctor a celebrity, and he resigns from Voyager to stay, only to be replaced by a hologram with an impossible vocal range.
voy-6x14: Returning from an away mission, Paris, Kim, Chakotay, and Neelix relive a massacre they never saw, memories broadcast by an alien monument so the atrocity is never forgotten.
voy-6x15: Kidnapped by the promoter Penk, Seven is forced to fight in the tsunkatse arena, where an aging Hirogen trains her while she waits for rescue.
voy-6x16: Adolescent Borg drones cut off from the Collective hold Chakotay, Paris, Kim, and Neelix hostage on their cube, and Seven must reach the children before their leader acts.
voy-6x17: After the crew's careless holodeck changes, the villagers of Fair Haven decide their visitors are spirit folk and turn on them, holding the Doctor captive.
voy-6x18: Lyndsay Ballard, killed three years earlier, returns transformed into a Kobali, the species that reproduces by reviving the dead, while Seven struggles to parent the rebellious Borg children.
voy-6x19: Seven returns Icheb to his Brunali parents, but her suspicions prove right: they engineered him as a living weapon against the Borg and mean to use him again.
voy-6x20: Janeway takes three struggling crewmen, including the hypochondriac Telfer and the aloof Harren, on a Delta Flyer mission that turns dangerous amid dark matter.
voy-6x21: Con artists posing as Janeway, Tuvok, and Chakotay swindle alien trading partners in Voyager's name, and the real crew runs a sting to catch them.
voy-6x22: Stranded after a shuttle crash, Torres becomes the muse of Kelis, a poet in a pre-industrial society who turns her tales of Voyager into plays for his patron.
voy-6x23: An aged, embittered Kes travels back to her first year aboard Voyager and helps the Vidiians attack it, determined to take her younger self home to Ocampa.
voy-6x24: Transmitted home through the Pathfinder array, the Doctor tries to treat his dying creator, Lewis Zimmerman, who scorns the outdated program he built.
voy-6x25: During a blackout, Neelix tells the Borg children the story behind it: an electromagnetic lifeform taken from its nebula that seized Voyager's systems in its desperation to return.
voy-6x26: Seven discovers Unimatrix Zero, a shared dream world where drones live as individuals during regeneration, and Janeway lets herself be assimilated to help it resist the Borg Queen.
voy-7x01: Deliberately assimilated, Janeway, Torres, and Tuvok spread a nanovirus that lets Unimatrix Zero's drones keep their individuality while awake, igniting a resistance the Borg Queen cannot crush.
voy-7x02: When Seven's cortical node begins to fail, she faces death with unexpected fear, and young Icheb offers his own implant to save her despite the risk to himself.
voy-7x03: In a race marking a new peace, Tom Paris flies the Delta Flyer and strains things with Torres, as a rival plots sabotage, before the couple finally marries.
voy-7x04: Tuvok hunts whoever is attacking Voyager's former Maquis, unaware a Bajoran fanatic has conditioned him through a letter from home to be the attacker and lead a mutiny.
voy-7x05: Stolen and sold to a hospital ship that rations care by social status, the Doctor defies its callous administrator, secretly treating the poor and even infecting him.
voy-7x06: A holographic Barclay arrives through the Pathfinder link with a route home, but Ferengi have rigged him to lead the crew to their deaths for Seven's Borg implants.
voy-7x07: When Lokirrim forces attack the Delta Flyer, the Doctor hides his program inside Seven's implants and indulges her senses, while aboard Voyager Tuvok battles his pon farr.
voy-7x08: Harry Kim gets his first command aboard a crippled Kraylor ship posing as a medical transport, while Icheb misreads Torres's friendly interest as romance.
voy-7x09-10: Holographic prey built with technology Janeway gave the Hirogen turn on their hunters, and the Doctor sides with their Bajoran leader, Iden, until Iden's crusade turns fanatical.
voy-7x11: A temporal rift splinters Voyager into different eras, and Chakotay recruits a Janeway from before the ship was stranded to mend it, dodging Seska, macroviruses, and Chaotica.
voy-7x12: Pregnant with a daughter, Torres fears the child will suffer for her Klingon traits as she did growing up, and secretly tries to alter the baby's genes.
voy-7x13: Voyager takes aboard Nygean prisoners bound for execution, and when the Doctor cures a killer's brain defect and he feels remorse, the crew questions the death penalty.
voy-7x14: Descendants of Klingon pilgrims who have wandered for a century decide Torres's unborn daughter is their prophesied savior, bringing their feuds and a deadly virus aboard Voyager.
voy-7x15: Trapped in a void where stranded ships survive by preying on one another, Janeway builds a cooperative alliance, helped by Fantome, an alien who communicates through music.
voy-7x16: Most of Voyager's crew is abducted and memory-wiped into laborers on the planet Quarra, where Janeway falls for a coworker, while Chakotay, Kim, and Neelix plot a rescue.
voy-7x17: Chakotay goes undercover in the Quarren workforce to restore his crewmates' memories as the authorities close in, and Janeway must choose between Voyager and her new love, Jaffen.
voy-7x18: Seven secretly explores emotions on the holodeck, including a romance with a simulated Chakotay, until a Borg failsafe in her implants shuts her feelings down.
voy-7x19: To save his teenage son from expulsion by the Continuum, Q leaves him with Janeway to learn discipline, and the boy's reckless pranks endanger the crew.
voy-7x20: When a publisher releases the Doctor's holonovel, a thinly veiled attack on the crew, without his consent, an arbitration hearing weighs whether a hologram can own his work.
voy-7x21: Sent by Starfleet to recover the 21st-century probe Friendship One, Voyager finds its antimatter knowledge helped devastate an alien world, whose survivors take hostages and kill Joe Carey.
voy-7x22: Crash-landed inside a force field protecting the primitive Ventu, Chakotay and Seven befriend the tribe, while Tom Paris serves a traffic-safety sentence for speeding on Ledos.
voy-7x23: Finding a Talaxian settlement in an asteroid field threatened by miners, Neelix helps it hold its ground and decides to stay with Dexa and her son.
voy-7x24: Hierarchy aliens abduct Janeway and demand Voyager's warp core, so the Doctor impersonates crewmates one after another to steal it, then must confess his deceptions.
voy-7x25-26: Admiral Janeway travels back from the 2400s with armor and a plan to bring Voyager home through a Borg transwarp hub, sacrificing herself to cripple the Borg Queen.
vst-1x01: A dangerous Klingon assault becomes even harder to handle when the crew gets tangled up in an unfortunate choice of words.
vst-1x02: A shipboard holiday party takes an unusual turn when a Vulcan is put in charge of providing the entertainment.
vst-1x03: A first contact between strangers turns out to be every bit as awkward as a bad first date.
vst-1x04: Holodeck hijinks take center stage in a comic short that stacks one hologram upon another.
vst-1x05: The old guard crosses paths with a new generation, and bruised feelings and short tempers follow in a brief comic sketch.
